meetings.summary: The Lunenburg Board of Assessors met after extended technical/audio difficulties delayed the start. The principal assessor gave a lengthy status report covering chapter land compliance issues, a resident inquiry that uncovered dozens of undocumented property depreciation ("obsolescence") adjustments needing review, preliminary FY2026 growth figures, cyclical inspection mailings, and new billing duties added to the office; the board also discussed updating the outdated 41A tax deferral income limit, the senior tax exemption program, and scheduling for RFP review and future meetings.

Blue postcards were mailed to residents due for inspection this cycle; only those who received a card will be visited.
The office received a surge of resident calls about the cyclical inspection notices.

budget_items.topic: Interim adjustments contract with Vision Appraisal
budget_items.what_was_said: Vision is contracted to deliver interim value adjustments by a September deadline and has assured the office it will be on time this year, unlike the prior year.

The assessor gave preliminary FY2026 growth figures, noting personal property values are not yet complete pending appraisals from utility companies; growth is described as much lower than the prior year with no comparison figure available.

budget_items.topic: Obsolescence coding discovered on a resident inquiry
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident's property value question led staff to discover an unexplained 20% economic obsolescence code, prompting a review that found many properties with external or functional obsolescence adjustments needing justification.

The principal assessor and a board member were revising a three-year RFP scope of work with the town counsel's added insurance and compliance requirements; the board discussed doing inspections themselves rather than relying on a vendor for consistency.
The board found the income cap for the property tax deferral program has not been updated since it was set, and agreed to draft a warrant article to revise it for the next town meeting.

budget_items.topic: Senior means-tested real estate tax exemption (41D)
budget_items.what_was_said: Eligibility requires age 65+, 15 years of residency, circuit breaker credit qualification, and income/asset limits; the maximum exemption for FY2026 was stated, and applicants may also qualify for an elderly exemption in the same year.
The board discussed printing a batch of brochures for the senior exemption program once a revised version is ready.

budget_items.what_was_said: The office was assigned motor vehicle and real estate billing file responsibilities in Munis in addition to existing duties, straining limited staff hours.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors agreed to set up a subcommittee to work out the process for the new senior means-tested tax exemption, with a target of two months or less.
Members agreed to review neighborhood and site-index values in house, starting with the lake properties, and to implement nothing until the review is done.
Most of the meeting went to editing a public presentation on senior exemptions and deferrals; the senior circuit breaker pages were pulled out and a HERO Act bullet added.
Members said the new senior exemption would probably be paid for from the overlay, possibly raising it, and deferred that question to February 5th.
The principal assessor will draft a placeholder warrant article on exemption income and asset limits for the next meeting. No formal votes were audible.

why_it_matters: A new senior means-tested exemption is likely to be paid for from the overlay, the reserve for abatements and exemptions, so the cost could be spread across other taxpayers' bills rather than appearing as a separate line.
A review of site-index values for lake properties could change how those homes are assessed, though the board said nothing will take effect until the review is finished.
Updated exemption income and asset limits would likely need a warrant article, which is a vote residents may be asked to take at town meeting.
watch_next: February 5th meeting: overlay discussion, the draft placeholder warrant article on exemption limits, and a check with town counsel on funding the senior exemption.
